result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers recommend free, OFL-licensed sans-serifs, self-host them, cover print with embedded fonts and give fallback stacks that end in sans-serif. B says which fallbacks ship on Android and on library Windows machines, and it asks for a check on an old Android phone and a library computer, though it skips a test print. A never says to check on real devices and makes a shaky claim that library computers 'can't load much.' | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers recommend a suitable free, OFL-licensed body face, self-host it, and cover web and print with embedded PDFs. A wins mainly because it tells the reader to test real text on an old Android phone and a library computer. B never suggests testing on real devices or doing a test print. B gives stronger device-specific readability advice, such as avoiding light weights on cheap screens and photocopies, but its claim that locked-down library computers 'can't load much' is shaky. Neither answer clearly says which fallback faces can't be assumed, and A lists Helvetica Neue without noting it isn't on Android or Windows.
